cards.title: Read the architecture
items: A follows an API-key agent turn and task creation. I follows the Islands workspace and its services. D follows direct island auto-tags. B follows screen memory and proposed tasks. J is the separate Execubriiz worker.

Repeated factory, provider and database boxes are the same runtime roles at different call sites. Region boxes mark process or ownership slices; they do not imply extra sandboxes. Click any component for revision-pinned source evidence.

cards.title: Islands identity and data migration
items: The Islands workspace now uses Islands names throughout the renderer, Electron IPC, database and theme selectors. Migration 017 renames saved project tables and task links in place, keeping existing project data available.

Older projects become islands on load, with files grouped into Docs/Code and Media cards and a migration journal entry. No files move. The store serializes version 2; saveIslandState writes the desks/templates view payload through the Islands API.

cards.title: Desks, cards and rendering
items: A desk holds a manual selection or rule-based view of shared islands, with its own camera, positions, dim setting and card visibility. The same island can appear on several desks. Hiding Agent cards only hides their presentation.

Cards cover Monetize, Terminal, Webview, Thoughts/Discussions, Media, Agent, Docs/Code, Goals/Todo, Visual Planning and Ship/Finish. Islands and cards have reusable templates and a chosen main card. Off-screen islands are culled; webviews mount only near the visible area.

cards.title: One Islands journal, two entrances
items: Opening the journal from an island scopes its log and chapter to that project; the calendar retains other islands with faded entries. Opening Islands from the Journals shelf shows all projects through the same store.

This journal reads island entries, shared auto-tag / Hunter changes, milestones, deadlines and ship dates. It does not use the ordinary journal entry tables or Execubriiz worker. Auto-tags retain undo; File Hunter results still require selection.

cards.title: Island agents use the task system
items: An Agent card saves the island, creates a task linked by islandProjectId, then enables automation. The app-window listener obtains the task permission choice and dispatches an accepted run to the main AutomationRunner. Task updates feed the card; pause, resume and answers use the same task.

Closing a desk or hiding Agent cards is not a pause command. The local task entry flow and renderer tools still depend on the main app window. Main-runner existence alone does not prove window-independent completion.

cards.title: References, owned documents and archives
items: Imported files stay where they are and appear as references. FileHawk checks missing paths and can locate moved files. Docs/Code previews originals; its save endpoint restricts writes by a lexical path check beneath userData/Islands. That check is not a symlink-canonicalization claim.

App-created documents live under userData/Islands. Archive creates a dated ZIP under Documents/briizOS Island Archives, copying source files and reporting missing paths. The old consolidate IPC still exists, but Islands uses islandArchiveIsland.

cards.title: Terminal and Webview are working cards
items: Terminal cards call islandTerminalRun directly. Main launches a login shell through /usr/bin/script, streams output, retains a bounded replay buffer, and stops children on app quit. This path does not call ToolContext or the agent terminal approval gate.

Webview cards use persist:island, unload when off-screen, and can restart their linked terminal command when a page fails. Terminal output supports colors and progress, but is not a full terminal emulator for screen-redrawing applications.

cards.title: Updated model request adapters
items: The checked-in profile catalog now includes GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, Claude 5.5 and Gemini 3.8 Flash; retired IDs include Gemini 3.7 Flash and gemini-omni-flash. These are repository configuration facts, not a claim of current provider availability.

The model factory routes GPT-5.6/GPT-6 through Responses and forwards GPT-6 reasoning through the installed adapter. It rejects none for GPT-6.1 Sol, uses adaptive thinking for Claude 5.5, and omits custom sampling for Gemini. Provider selection and content-consent boundaries remain distinct.

cards.title: Renderer ownership
items: React owns panels, shell layout, appContext and the live tool registry. Main owns structured writes; data:changed reloads renderer state. ThemeProvider/Chromap work from AppCombined.css.
The mounted Sources activity view is the actual log UI in this checkout; AGENTS.md names LogPanel.jsx, but that file is absent. Media playback and recorder session history are distinct features.

cards.title: Approval levels are narrower than their labels
items: Graph ask-always interrupts only tools in DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS. Renderer ask-always checks requiresConfirmation; read-only tools and openCanvas can proceed. Unknown threads use this same rule, not deny-everything.

ask-destructive lets briizos_* mutations pass the graph; renderer exempts its reversible UI set, while other flagged mutations still ask. no-asking disables confirmation but the renderer still checks configured paths.

cards.title: Approval integrity gaps
items: ToolContext trusts __agentGraphConfirmed to skip confirmation; it is forwarded in renderer params rather than bound to a main-owned one-use authorization. Blacklist checks still precede that flag.

confirmAction invokes the handler directly with edited params; it does not rerun the per-surface gate. bridge.js accepts tool results by requestId without checking reply sender. Raw filesystem/terminal/structured IPC also skips the renderer executor.

cards.title: Shell and path gates are heuristic
items: Renderer isDestructiveCommand returns safe for a recognized first verb before checking compound commands or redirection. Graph parsing examines separators first, but treats node, python, git, curl and other powerful tools as safe verbs.

Blacklists compare strings before main resolves paths. ~/ expansion, .. components and symlinks are not canonicalized by these checks. Shell arguments are not comprehensively governed by the filesystem blacklist. These are code-based limitations, not exploit-test results.

cards.title: Screen-text consent has a second route
items: Briizy assistants require cloudTextAnalysisAllowed and the pixel/path-pattern scan. The main agent tools search_screen_memory and get_recent_activity read saved OCR without that flag, then return it as model-visible tool output.

The egress scanner catches known data URI, image magic, binary buffers and selected POSIX path forms. It is a pattern filter, not a universal prohibition on sensitive text or arbitrary path encodings.

cards.title: Capture controls and actual enforcement
items: Capture defaults off; cloud text analysis defaults off. setConfig({enabled:true}) can start the helper without checking onboardedAt. macOS Screen Recording remains an enforced native gate. Avatar visibility is independent of recording.

Automatic capture defaults to alternating active-window and full-display screenshots. Exclusions examine frontmost metadata; a permitted front window does not exclude other visible windows from the display image.

cards.title: Direct calls do not inherit chat policy
items: Island auto-tags use the shared store queue and Background helpers model route. File-path changes trigger excerpt reads. Tags feed search and desk rules; the journal records changes and offers undo. These direct calls do not enter ToolContext.

A configured model/key is a readiness condition. It does not authorize every external transmission. createChatModel checks profiles/adapters/credentials and rejects Codex subscription calls; it does not centralize content consent.

cards.title: Background helpers and routing
items: The graph adds title, tags, memory extraction and summarization calls when their hook conditions allow. Model selection order is call-site specific; title/memory helpers can inherit the active model ahead of Background routing.

Briizy assistants use their own configured model or app default; base.callModel does not consult the Background route. Execubriiz uses journal model settings, then live/deep AI route, then app default.

cards.title: Journal-specific authority
items: Execubriiz starts with full intensity and unpaused preferences. Private entries are filtered in code; Invisible entries may be supplied to the model and withheld from visible source citations.

Schema/budget/generation/revision/protected/fixed checks govern journal commits. Some content edits apply automatically; structural edits become proposals. Full curation can enqueue web research only when the context has no Invisible material. General chat/task permissions do not govern this worker.

cards.title: Embedded content is a weak boundary
items: Canvas srcDoc permits scripts with same-origin and forms. The URL probe checks its payload/probeId, but not event.origin or event.source. Same-origin scripted content weakens separation from the privileged parent; exact reach is inferred and was not exercised.

Main disables webSecurity and allows insecure content in development, skips CSP injection there, and enables webviewTag. Production CSP still includes unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval. This map does not claim a tested exploit or an isolated canvas security sandbox.

cards.title: Codex is a distinct child process
items: Selecting a Codex profile spawns the installed codex app-server --stdio and uses its ChatGPT OAuth. thread/start and resume request read-only sandbox with approvalPolicy never. Those controls are owned by the installed CLI.
BriizOS forwards text deltas from that provider; this adapter does not wire the renderer tool bridge or dynamic tools. General createChatModel explicitly refuses Codex subscription models.

cards.title: Cloud ownership and remote execution
items: Renderer Firebase Auth supplies UID, project ID and token to CloudGateway. Main checks required fields and confirms rebinding, then uses bearer-authenticated Firestore REST. Server security rules and external web/mobile producers are outside electron/ and src/ evidence.

Primary lease, target device, schema/kind, expiry and deduplication gate command intake. Accepted remote execute_task commands auto-dispatch without a fresh local start approval; task ceiling and subsequent tool interruptions still apply. Device lease coordination uses reads/writes, not an atomic lock.

cards.title: Storage and observability
items: Main initializes userData/briizos.db with better-sqlite3, WAL and foreign keys. Structured writes use transactions/revisions; logs, AI audit, checkpoints, operation receipts and encrypted secrets share this authority. Captured pixels live in the local rewind archive.

safeStorage fails closed when encryption is unavailable for saved secrets. Environment API keys take precedence for model calls. Operation receipts deduplicate effects; they are not human approvals. Graph initial audit storage is required before send, while direct helpers have their own narrower logs.

cards.title: External dependencies and dormant code
items: Runtime packages: Electron + Node, React/ReactDOM, LangGraph/LangChain adapters, Zod, better-sqlite3, Firebase, Tiptap, theme PostCSS, React DnD, Three/GSAP. See package.json and the component source passports.

GitHub REST reads are implemented. Google Drive OAuth/list/download are explicit placeholders. iCloud and USB are mounted filesystem access. Native Studio/site launches are external handoffs. Legacy agent Python and old local-db/Firestore modules exist, but they are not the main agent/persistence paths traced here.
